title: QUIC: fix handling of Key Update
description:
After a key update, we should update Packet Protection cipher but we shouldn't touch the Header Protection one.

With the current code, PP and HP ciphers are quite entangled and we always reset both of them. Therefore, at the second key update we reset the used 1-RTT HP cipher too; no wonder even header decryption fails from that point on.

To properly fix this issue, all the ciphers structures has been rewritten, clearly separating PP code from HP one.

Close #16920 

Close #16916

notes.body: assigned to @Lekensteyn
LGTM, @Lekensteyn can you check ?

Ah right... `quic_cipher_reset` clears the HP cipher too. There is already a TODO comment in the `quic_cipher` structure definition about the "proper" refactoring needed (client/server HP ciphers for the three different encryption levels in `quic_info_data`, plus one for the appdata HP cipher in `quic_pp_state`).

Do you want to give that a go or should I prepare a patch?

Do you want the ciphers stuff to be refactored in this patch or as a follow-up? I am asking because this fix should be back-ported to 3.4, IMO, and I don't know if you intend to back-port only the fix itself or the entire refactoring...

I intend to backport the refactoring with the fix to keep the difference smaller between 3.4 and master. Otherwise there might be additional conflicts as we try to backport more stuff later on.

@alagoutte what do you think? Should we merge this patch as-is and work on a follow-up refactoring, or just go straight for the refactoring? I am inclined to do the latter for the previous reason.
Oups sorry for delay, it is a big refactor ? because i will be nice to master and 3.4 with no big difference...

changed this line in [version 2 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/730/diffs?diff_id=123162557&start_sha=6da7117708cb002bfd0f721486000294d6d88f95#d4fb11677787b1f9a3875d35bb865f4ba9d238ee_2401_2481)
Looks reasonable to me!
What the status ? wait for the refactor ?
Yes, waiting for @IvanNardi to push the new patch described above.

Refactoring pushed: it is quite large...

There are 3 basic cipher structures now: for all of them a _init(), _is_initialized(), _prepare() and a _reset() function is defined.

A lot of variables and function parameters names have been updated to clearly indicate which cipher they are referring to.

Doing this refactoring correctly has been easy; up to you guys to decide if it has been done well too!
LGTM @Lekensteyn it is ok ?
LGTM, maybe some newlines could be added, but functionally it looks reasonable so I'll just merge it. I did not test, but I assume that you did verify that the problem was addressed :)
